calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 9 Nov, FV $1,531) — his pick over TSM: record 80%+ operating margins two quarters running, longer-term customer contracts now dampen the old price volatility, and even with FCF growth peaking ~2028-29 the DCF still shows ~2x upside. He owns it.
calls.base_case: Longer-term contracts (price floor/ceiling) smooth the memory cycle; FCF growth peaks ~2028-29 then grows slowly.
calls.bull_case: Hyperscaler demand stays ahead of supply and pricing holds at record levels.
calls.bear_case: Peak-cycle earnings: the 3.5x P/E is peak EPS and margins collapse when the cycle turns, as in 2024 (-40% operating margin).

calls.bull_case: Wall Street's 2028 earnings peak proves too pessimistic; HBM pricing power holds and the stock doubles toward $1,600.
calls.bear_case: Capex-growth peak compresses multiples; new supply or a memory innovation breaks pricing power and the stock halves.

Moat is weaker than NVDA's (why NVDA ranks higher), but the margin of safety still warrants buying.

calls.bull_case: Supply/demand imbalance persists at extreme margins; FV $1,400 implies ~42% upside.
calls.bear_case: Price-range clauses in long-term customer agreements could cut ASPs as SK Hynix/Samsung/CXMT competition builds; 80%+ margins invite rivals.

calls.bull: Memory shortages persist into 2028-2029, ASPs stay elevated, capex acceleration signals demand visibility.
calls.bear: Cycle turns; oversupply returns and earnings compress as the 5.8x multiple implies.
